info.title: LEPIC wallet API
info.description:
HTTP API of `lepic serve` for one LEPIC wallet.
**One wallet per serve.** Every path is relative to `/api/v1` and names no wallet. To serve several wallets, run one `lepic serve` per wallet, each with its own socket and port.

**Transports.** Two ways in. The Unix socket `lepic.sock` is readable only by the user who runs serve; there are no tokens, and OpenAPI cannot express it, so it has no security scheme here. Optional mutual TLS 1.3 (`--owner-tls`) admits clients listed in `api-clients` by key (`ownerTls`), each with one role: `read`, `receive` (also create invoices, addresses and links; never spends) or `full`. A call above a client role answers 403 with code `role_required`. The socket is always `full`. Operations marked `x-socket-only: true` (`PUT /wallet/password`, `POST /contacts/export`, `POST /contacts/import`) answer 403 with code `socket_only` over TLS. Over TLS, `POST /payments` needs a caller-chosen `id`.

**Wire protocols outside this API.** `/v2/foreign` (stock wallets, JSON-RPC) and `/api/v1/inbox` (LEPIC native) are the endpoints other wallets call. They are wire protocols and are not described here.

**Conventions.** Field names are snake_case; amounts are decimal strings in EPIC with up to 8 decimals; times are RFC 3339 UTC; optional fields are left out when empty, never null; enum values are lower snake_case and clients must accept values they do not know. Lists return `{items, next_cursor}`. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents. Besides the statuses each operation lists, any call may answer 408 `body_too_slow` or 413 `body_too_large` while serve reads its body, and 500 `internal` on a bug. On the socket, a request that carries the `x-lepic-*` headers of a forwarded CLI command answers 409 `serve_version_differs` or `serve_settings_differ` when they name another version or other settings than serve runs with; other clients do not send them. Every response carries `x-lepic-version`.

Refresh against the node and collect from the relays now.
Collect from the relays, or refresh against the node, more often for a while.
post.description: Runs the poller every `interval_seconds` for `duration_seconds` from now, then goes back to its base interval (30 s for `relays`, 60 s for `node`). A boost that overlaps the poller's running one keeps the later end and the shorter interval. The interval is at least 5 s and the duration at most 600 s: values outside are clamped, and the answer is the window that took effect. Serve boosts `relays` for 120 s at 5 s by itself after `POST /payments`, `POST /contacts`, `POST /pair-requests/{id}/accept` and `POST /links`.

post.summary: Start a payment: a send or an invoice.
post.description:
Starts a send (`kind: send`, default) or an invoice (`kind: invoice`). Returns 201, or 200 with the stored payment on an idempotent repeat (same `id`, same body). A different body with the same `id` is 409 `idempotency_mismatch`; a repeat while the first call runs is 409 `in_progress`. Over owner TLS `id` is required.

`to` forms: `key@host` (Epicbox address), `http://` or `https://` URL, `.onion` address, `epic:` link, `contact:ID`, `account:LABEL`.

200.description: Idempotent repeat: the stored payment; no money moved.

The event log: a JSON page after `after`, or a live stream.
get.description: As JSON, a page oldest first after `after`, with `next_cursor` as for any list. With `Accept: text/event-stream`, a live stream that resumes from `Last-Event-ID` or `?after=`. Events are kept 30 days by default; a client that asks for older ids first gets `events.skipped` with the count.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return events with an id greater than this.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma list of event types; `payment.*` style wildcards allowed.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Stream resume point: the sequence number of the last event received.

200.description: A page of events, or a live stream.

schema.description: Server-sent events (WHATWG). Each frame has `id:` the event's sequence number, `event:` its type, and `data:` the Event as JSON, then a blank line. A comment line (`: keepalive`) is sent every 15 seconds to keep idle connections open.

ownerTls.description: Mutual TLS 1.3 with a client key listed in `api-clients` (`--owner-tls`). Each client has one role (`read`, `receive` or `full`); every operation names its minimum in `x-role`. The Unix socket needs no credentials, has the `full` role, and is described in `info.description`. The empty security requirement `{}` means the socket.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: Opaque cursor from `next_cursor`. Other query parameters must stay the same across pages.

Forbidden.description: Not allowed (403): code `socket_only` over TLS, or `role_required` when the TLS client role is too low.

Conflict.description: Conflict with the object's state or an idempotency key (409).

Unprocessable.description: Valid but impossible, e.g. insufficient funds or invoice changed (422).

BadGateway.description: The node or a relay failed (502).

Unavailable.description: Not ready: scan running or serve stopping (503). May set Retry-After.

GatewayTimeout.description: The node or a relay timed out (504).

Decimal.description: EPIC amount as a decimal string

to.description: Address, URL, onion, contact id, or the relay used.

text.description: Paste, show as QR, or save as a file.

id.description: The slate id; the other wallet sees the same.

kind.description: Who started it; unknown = found by a scan.

direction.description: self = between own accounts, or splitting own coins.

state_reason.description: Why it reached an end state: by_us, by_them, superseded, ...

account.description: Label; for self, the account it left.

balance_change.description: Signed change to this wallet's balance, fee included.

our_address.description: Which of our addresses it reached.

link_id.description: For a payment taken at one of this wallet's epic1 links: the link's id, as `GET /links` lists it. A link's id is used again after the link is retired.

purpose.description: Set by the sender, between contacts.

check_code.description: Payer side of an in-person code, once delivered.

actions.description: The calls that work on this payment now, as the wallet computes them. A call not listed fails with 409 `action_not_available`. Clients must accept values they do not know.

cancellable_from_height.description: A posted send the chain never took.

metadata.description: Local only, never sent. Up to 50 keys; keys up to 40 and values up to 500 characters.

handoff.description: In create and open responses, when you deliver by hand.

seal.description: Files to this contact are sealed.

requested_relay.description: They asked you to move there. Answer with `POST /contacts/{id}/move`.

refused_relay.description: A move you refused. The contact was not told.

state.description: Absent until the listener reports one.

failures.description: Failures in a row; 0 after a success.
Failures in a row; 0 after a success.

requests.description: Requests this serve answered since it started.

in_flight.description: Requests and event streams being answered.

peer.description: For addresses, after asking the relay.

payment_id.description: When it belongs to a payment this wallet knows.

expect.description: Optional guard. Anything whose inspection `type` is not listed is refused with 422 `unexpected_input` and nothing changes.

handoff.description: The answer to give back by hand, in the format that came in.

type.description: `resource.what_happened`. An open set: new types may be added, and clients must skip types they do not know. Known types: payment.created, payment.state_changed, payment.updated, payment.confirmations_reached, contact.created, contact.state_changed, contact.updated, contact.removed, pair_request.received, payload.received, quarantine.added, account.balance_changed, wallet.progress, relay.updated, slate.unmatched, events.skipped.

reason.description: Why: for `*.state_changed` the end-state reason; for `slate.unmatched` `unknown_slate` or `notice`; for `events.skipped` `lagged` or `pruned`; for `relay.updated` `home_unreachable` or the transport's reason.

changed.description: The top-level fields of `object` that changed (`*.updated`, `relay.updated`).

payment_id.description: `payment.state_changed` for a payment the wallet no longer holds, such as a parked invoice that expired.

contact_id.description: `quarantine.added`, `payload.received`, and `contact.state_changed` for a contact the wallet no longer holds.

stage.description: `slate.unmatched`: the slate's stage, such as `S2` or `I2`.

sender.description: `slate.unmatched`: where it came from, as the relay reported it.

target_height.description: `wallet.progress`: the height the scan runs to.

count.description: `events.skipped`: how many events the reader missed.

param.description: JSON pointer to the bad field.

example.title: Unprocessable Content
example.detail: The account has 1.2 EPIC spendable; the payment needs 1.507 with the fee.

id.description: Optional caller-chosen id. A send uses it as its slate id, and so does an invoice given a version-4 UUID; an invoice given another UUID takes a slate id of the wallet's own and keeps this one as an alias that `GET /payments/{id}` also answers. Read `id` from the answer. Idempotency key: a repeat with the same id and body returns the stored payment with 200; a different body is 409 `idempotency_mismatch`. Required over owner TLS.

to.description: Destination. Forms: `key@host` (Epicbox address); `http://` or `https://` URL; `.onion` address; `epic:` link; `contact:ID`; `account:LABEL` (own account). Without `to`, `via` must be `file` or `in_person`.

via.description: Route. Same values as Payment.via; `file` and `in_person` produce a handoff.

account.description: Account label; default account when absent.

message.description: Signed into the slate, at most 256 bytes. Shows as `message` on this payment and as `their_message` on the other party's, an invoice to a contact included.

change_outputs.description: Number of change outputs; `account:default` with 3 splits coins.

ttl_blocks.description: Blocks after which the other party must refuse the slate. For a send, a V2 slate (Epicbox, HTTP) has no TTL field: the wallet keeps the height and expires the send at refresh if it is still unanswered. For an invoice, the I1 carries it, the payment shows it as `expires_at_height`, and a refresh past it expires the invoice.

relay_ok.description: Allow delivery to a relay outside your list.

legacy.description: true: give an http(s):// or onion payee the V2 or V3 slate every wallet takes, even when its listener offers native slates (today's `tx send --legacy`).

deliver.description: false: create the payment and return the handoff only.

metadata.description: Local notes, never sent. The bounds are input validation, not policy.

links.description: Read every link mailbox after a restore.

metadata.description: A key set to the empty string is removed.

amount.description: The invoice amount, retyped; must match.

answer_id.description: The answer that finishes the payment (in-person codes can get up to 16).

relay.description: `next` for the next relay, or a relay host.

to.description: `contact:ID`: send a slate through a contact's mailbox, for example a withdrawal.

account.description: Account label; default account when absent.

deliver.description: false: return the reply to send by hand.

data_base64.description: Up to 16 KiB of bytes, base64-encoded.

document.description: The pairing records as a backup document (opaque).

host.description: The relay the user was shown; must equal the contact's `requested_relay`.

poller.description: `relays`: the collect from the contact, pairing and link mailboxes. `node`: the wallet refresh.

duration_seconds.description: How long the boost lasts from now; at most 600.

interval_seconds.description: How often the poller runs meanwhile; at least 5.

poller.description: `relays`: the collect from the contact, pairing and link mailboxes. `node`: the wallet refresh.

until.description: When the poller goes back to its base interval.
